name: Diagonal Gradient Flow (Cross Gradient)
description: The chainsaw for diagonal fractures. The supreme enemy of Generative Diffusion models. When AI attempts to mathematically interpolate and render diagonal geometric structures, it frequently suffers from microscopic 'melting' or 'staircasing'. This measurement ignores straight horizontal or vertical alignments, exclusively slicing the image across biased diagonal axes to hunt down unnatural intensity flow disruptions.
algorithm: Cross-directional Gradient Variance & Hessian Matrix Tracking
mechanism: The algorithm computes first and second-order morphological derivatives exclusively along the 45-degree and 135-degree axes. In an authentic optical photograph, light scatters smoothly across all diagonals. Conversely, AI-generated imagery (or synthetically upscaled elements) routinely feature violently crashing diagonal gradients, creating dead zones or razor-sharp, non-optical micro-fractures.
parameters: Operator: Cross-Scharr/Sobel Derivatives, Variance Tracker: Hessian Feature Matrix, Domain: High-Frequencies
accuracy: Solid (70-79%) - A specialized drill designed specifically to penetrate the camouflage of diagonally complex details (clothing wrinkles, hair strands) mangled by AI rendering.
source: Digital Image Forensics & Computational Photography Networks
useCase: Scrutinizes structural continuity on a slant, immediately triggering an alarm when a formerly smooth diagonal curve suddenly fragments into synthetic microscopic jagged pixels—the hallmark of AI convolutional failures.

references.title: Barni, M. et al. (2010). Forensic analysis of digital images: Spatial contrast and cross-gradient inconsistency.
Gonzalez, R.C. & Woods, R.E. (2018). Digital Image Processing. 4th Edition. Pearson.
Fridrich, J. & Kodovsky, J. (2012). Rich Models for Steganalysis of Digital Images. IEEE TIFS.

strengths:
• Hyper-sensitive to complex interlacing structures (chain-link fences, steel meshes) that generative AI almost universally fails to render with 100% geometric optical precision.
• Lightning-fast execution, requiring zero heavy-duty neural model inferencing to execute its sweeps.
limitations:
• The forensic blade completely slips if the image suffers from heavy Gaussian blurring or severe out-of-focus bokeh, which naturally obliterates cross-gradient optics.
• Highly prone to firing False Positives on authentically captured complex diagonal patterns (e.g., sharp diagonal plaid shirts, diagonally tiled floors).
